## Correction to 1.19.0 — three members were pinned one release behind

**If you are on 1.19.0, upgrade.** 1.19.0's release notes stated that it advanced Workflow to
0.12.2, Bench to 0.6.2 and Experiment to 0.7.2. It did not. It shipped those three at **0.12.1,
0.6.1 and 0.7.1** — the versions from before the correction wave. Judge 0.15.2 and Journal 1.9.0
were pinned correctly.

1.19.1 pins what 1.19.0 claimed:

| Member | 1.19.0 pinned | 1.19.1 pins |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-judge` | 0.15.2 | 0.15.2 (unchanged) |
| `journal` | 1.9.0 | 1.9.0 (unchanged) |
| `agent-workflow` | **0.12.1** | **0.12.2** |
| `agent-bench` | **0.6.1** | **0.6.2** |
| `agent-experiment` | **0.7.1** | **0.7.2** |

Nothing else changed. The managed set remains the same 72 consumer-facing coordinates.

### Why this matters beyond tidiness

The point of the correction wave was that the resolved graph should carry **one** judge version
throughout. Agent Judge 0.15.0 and 0.15.1 could silently drop a judge from a parallel jury,
returning a verdict computed from fewer judges than it listed.

Repinning `agent-judge` alone does not achieve that. Workflow's `JudgeGate` evaluates steps through
a jury; Bench scores benchmark runs through juries; Experiment reaches the judge both directly and
transitively through Workflow. Because 1.19.0 left those three at their pre-wave versions, **a
consumer on 1.19.0 still resolves the defective judge transitively**, even though the BOM appears to
carry the fix. That is precisely the sibling-pin drift the wave existed to eliminate.

On 1.19.1 the graph is coherent: every path to Agent Judge resolves 0.15.2, and every path to Agent
Journal resolves 1.9.0.

### Provenance

`agent-workflow 0.12.2`, `agent-bench 0.6.2` and `agent-experiment 0.7.2` were published on
2026-08-25 through the certified consumer-rooted SBOM procedure, each with its independently
resolved consumer closure matching its published SBOM component-for-component, dependency SCA
green, and post-publication proof that the artifacts on Central are byte-identical to what was
certified. They existed before 1.19.0 was cut; the BOM simply failed to pin them.
